clue.text: Worriedly describes lacking credit in any case

indicators.note: worriedly suggests agitation, so the letters of the word describes are jumbled

parts.note: CR is the standard abbreviation for credit on a bank statement

explanation.surface: Someone anxiously portrays a person short of money, whatever happens.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'lacking credit' as being broke, but it marks the deletion that comes before the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases are adverbial fillers meaning anyway or moreover, used to add a further point.

clue.text: A clergyman's quiet work under British institute

indicators.note: under places these pieces below the British institute letters in a down entry

parts.note: sh is a call for quiet
op is short for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: A priest's silent research carried out beneath a British academic body.
explanation.definitionFit: A bishop is a senior member of the clergy, overseeing a diocese.

clue.text: Feels hurt seeing pictures included in text message

indicators.note: included in puts the pictures word inside the message abbreviation

parts.note: SMS is a text message sent by phone
art means pictures and paintings

explanation.surface: Someone is upset after seeing images in a text.
explanation.definitionFit: To smart is to sting or feel a pang of hurt, so the third-person form fits.

clue.text: Tactful service might follow this

definitions.meaning: handling people with discretion and tact
the ... service is a country's body of overseas envoys

explanation.definitionFit: Diplomatic means tactful; the diplomatic service is staffed by ambassadors and envoys.

clue.text: Weep over unprotected Nero's grave

indicators.note: over places the weeping word above the rest in a down entry

parts.note: to sob is to weep

indicators.note: unprotected means stripped of its outer covering, so the outside letters of Nero go

explanation.surface: Mourners cry over the exposed tomb of a Roman emperor.
explanation.definitionFit: Grave as an adjective means serious and solemn, as sober does.

clue.text: Notice joker following almost all of drama

indicators.note: following places the joker's word after the shortened drama
almost all of says the final letter of the word for drama is dropped

parts.note: a play is a drama on stage
the joker is a playing card, so CARD

explanation.surface: A theatre poster announces a comedian appearing after most of the show.
explanation.definitionFit: A placard is a sign or poster displayed publicly, i.e. a notice.

clue.text: Care following delivery of mail to part of South Africa?

definitions.note: describes the noun phrase postnatal care, the adjective standing for it

parts.note: post is mail
Natal was a province of South Africa, now KwaZulu-Natal

explanation.surface: Looking after a parcel once it has been sent to a region of South Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'delivery' looks postal, but it is childbirth.
explanation.definitionFit: Postnatal describes the period after childbirth and the care given to mother and baby then.

clue.text: Crown service protecting millions

indicators.note: protecting means one piece surrounds the other to guard it

parts.note: an ace is an unreturnable tennis service

explanation.surface: Royal regalia guarded by a huge security operation.
explanation.definitionFit: The crown of something is its top or peak, which is what an acme is.

clue.text: One leapt high, as a Springbok

indicators.note: high suggests intoxication, so the letters of One leapt are scrambled

explanation.surface: Something jumped high like a leaping springbok.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Springbok' suggests a South African rugby player, but it is the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The springbok is a South African gazelle, an example of the antelope family.

clue.text: Boring, when crossing road for slow people

parts.note: boring means dull

indicators.note: crossing means the when word lies across the road abbreviation, enclosing it

parts.note: as can mean when, as in as I arrived

explanation.surface: A tedious account of dim people trying to cross the street.
explanation.definitionFit: Dullards are dim-witted, slow-thinking people.

clue.text: To put one's foot down is a duty of sorts

definitions.meaning: to bring a foot down heavily on the ground
... duty is a British tax on property and documents

explanation.definitionFit: Stamping is slamming a foot down; stamp duty is a UK tax, so the word names a duty.

clue.text: Lead, say from corrupt copper?

parts.note: base means morally low or corrupt
copper is an example of a metal

explanation.surface: A clue to a policeman taking a lead from a crooked colleague.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a policeman and 'Lead' like a tip-off; both are metals here.
explanation.definitionFit: Lead is an example of a non-precious metal of the type alchemists hoped to turn into gold.

clue.text: Torrent causing rambling group to lose leader during day trip

indicators.note: during puts the jumbled letters within the trip word

parts.note: an outing is a short excursion for the day

indicators.note: rambling means wandering about, so the remaining letters are rearranged
to lose leader drops the first letter of the word group

explanation.surface: A walking club's excursion loses its guide, prompting a flood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rambling group' looks like hikers, but 'rambling' is the anagram signal working on what is left once the group loses its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A torrent is a violent rush of water or words, which a great outflow also describes.

clue.text: Request that cuts enjoyment by half

indicators.note: cuts signals that part of the word for enjoyment is chopped off
by half says only the front four of its eight letters remain

parts.note: pleasure is enjoyment

explanation.surface: An appeal that reduces someone's fun by fifty per cent.
explanation.definitionFit: A plea is an earnest appeal or entreaty, so a request.

clue.text: Wiping out call after service bill

indicators.note: after puts the call word behind the service and bill pieces

parts.note: Mass is a church service
AC is short for account, a bill
to ring is to call on the phone

explanation.surface: Someone is cleaned out by a phone call once a church collection arrives.
explanation.definitionFit: Massacring means slaughtering in great numbers, or figuratively defeating utterly, so wiping out.

clue.text: Short acts perhaps rewritten with depth

indicators.note: with adds the depth abbreviation at the end
rewritten means the letters of acts perhaps are written out again in a new order

parts.note: D is a standard abbreviation for depth in measurements

explanation.surface: A playwright reworks some scenes to give them more depth.
explanation.definitionFit: Being short of money means lacking cash, the sense of this hyphenated adjective.

clue.text: Mysterious ghost ship's most interesting parts

indicators.note: mysterious suggests something unexplained, so the letters of ghost ship are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, the possessive adding no letter

explanation.surface: A phantom vessel's most fascinating features.
explanation.definitionFit: High spots are the best or most memorable moments of something.

clue.text: Do we act differently hugging female, being false?

indicators.note: hugging means the jumbled letters wrap round the female abbreviation
differently means the letters of Do we act are arranged in another way

explanation.surface: Asking whether people behave otherwise when embracing a woman, being insincere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'differently' turns DOWEACT into TWOACED, which wraps round F.
explanation.definitionFit: Two-faced describes a hypocrite who deceives, so someone insincere or false.

clue.text: Flowers reptile habitually consumes

parts.note: croc is short for crocodile, a reptile
uses means takes regularly, as of drugs

explanation.surface: Blooms that an animal eats as a matter of routine.
explanation.definitionFit: Crocuses are small spring flowers grown from corms.

clue.text: On form demographic group?

parts.note: a machine that is on is working
a school form is a class

explanation.surface: Asking whether people in good shape count as a social category.
explanation.definitionFit: The working class is a social stratum, a group used in demographic analysis; the question mark flags it as one example.

clue.text: Entertain disheartened rabble with good beer

indicators.note: disheartened means losing the heart, so only the outer letters of rabble stay

parts.note: ale is a kind of beer

explanation.surface: Cheering up a dejected mob with fine ale.
explanation.definitionFit: To regale people is to entertain or amuse them, often with stories or food.

clue.text: Cuts due to arrest on board ship

indicators.note: on board places the arrest word inside the steamship letters

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
to nick is British slang for to arrest

explanation.surface: Budget reductions follow a police arrest aboard a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Snicks are small cuts or nicks; in cricket a snick is a faint edge.

clue.text: Reality produced by fine performance

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine on pencils and grading
an act is a performance on stage

explanation.surface: Truth emerging from an excellent piece of acting.
explanation.definitionFit: A fact is something actually true, a piece of reality.

clue.text: Shield design of touch screen with no end of bother

indicators.note: design of suggests making a pattern, so the device's letters are rearranged
with no removes a letter from the device's name
end of picks the final letter of the word bother

explanation.surface: A coat of arms is drawn on a tablet display without any fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end of bother' is R; take it from TOUCHSCREEN, leaving TOUCHSCEEN, which 'design of' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: In heraldry an escutcheon is the shield bearing a coat of arms.

clue.text: Completely turn Jude's heart, capturing writer

indicators.note: capturing means the heart letters enclose the writer word
heart means the middle letters of the name Jude

parts.note: a pen is something to write with

explanation.surface: An author changes the heart of Jude completely.
explanation.walkthrough: The heart of JUDE is UD, which surrounds PEN.
explanation.definitionFit: To upend something is to set it on its end or turn it upside down.

clue.text: Nation secured by future prospects on the rise

indicators.note: on the rise says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A country whose future outlook is getting better.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'on the rise' means the letters read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Peru is a South American country, so a nation.

clue.text: Dish for bad loser in lawsuit?

indicators.note: in puts the jumbled letters inside the word for lawsuit

parts.note: a case is a lawsuit in court

indicators.note: bad suggests something wrong with the letters, so they are reordered

explanation.surface: Asking what food to serve a sore loser in court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad loser' reads as a sore loser, but 'bad' is the anagram signal for the letters of loser.
explanation.definitionFit: A casserole is a stew cooked slowly in a lidded pot, so a type of dish.

clue.text: Name for savings scheme account?

parts.note: an ISA is a British tax-free individual savings account

explanation.surface: A question about what to call a savings account.
explanation.definitionFit: Isaac is a man's first name, from the biblical son of Abraham.

clue.text: Talk about seconds on field event

indicators.note: on means the second piece is attached after the first

parts.note: the discus throw is an athletics field event

explanation.surface: An athletics commentator chats about split times at the throwing event.
explanation.definitionFit: To discuss something is to talk it over.

clue.text: People who understand Australians?

definitions.meaning: to dig is slang for to understand, so those who get it
Digger is informal for an Australian, especially a soldier

explanation.definitionFit: Slang 'dig' means grasp; 'digger' is a nickname for an Australian, first applied to soldiers in the First World War.
